items.detail: The **S&P 500** rose 0.19% to 7,666.45 on Thursday to start October, while the Nasdaq added just 0.04% to 26,871.60.
items.why: The 10-year yield hit 5.344%, its highest since 2002, then fell back, and Micron and Alphabet's new AI model lifted tech.

items.detail: S&P 500 futures rose **0.26%** early Friday ahead of the September jobs report, where economists expect about 84,000 new jobs.
items.why: This is the last big jobs reading before the Fed's October 28 decision, so it could swing rate-hike odds.

items.detail: Hong Kong's **Hang Seng** fell 2.48% on Friday as it reopened after a holiday, while Korea's Kospi lost about 1%.
items.why: A jump in oil on renewed US-Iran tensions raised fresh inflation fears across Asia.

items.detail: India's **Nifty 50** fell 0.88% to **22,421.95** on Thursday, its fourth straight loss, and markets are closed Friday for Gandhi Jayanti.
items.why: Investors fear the RBI could raise rates at its October 7 meeting, and high energy prices add to the pressure.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** rose about **0.8%** on Thursday and beat the S&P 500, a rebound after a September drop of more than 5%.
items.why: Falling Treasury yields eased borrowing-cost worries, which weigh hardest on small companies.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** traded near **$83,900** on Friday after briefly topping $84,000 on Thursday, still stuck below $85,000.
items.why: US crypto ETFs saw over $200 million in combined outflows on October 1, led by bitcoin funds.

items.detail: **Ether** edged up to about **$2,720** on Friday, still under its $2,800 ceiling.
items.why: Ether funds also had outflows, and high yields are keeping buyers cautious before the jobs report.

items.detail: **Solana** slipped back below $120 to about **$118**, after trading between roughly $117 and $122.50 over 24 hours.
items.why: Solana funds turned to outflows on October 1 after a strong September, so the rally lost steam.

items.detail: **Spot gold** rose about 0.5% on Thursday to around **$4,177** and held steady ahead of Friday's US jobs report.
items.why: Yields fell back from 2002 highs, but oil above $100 keeps Fed hike bets alive and limits gold's gains.

crossCuttingTheme: Brent oil is back above $100 as the US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz drags on, keeping inflation and Fed hike fears alive and limiting gains in stocks, crypto and gold ahead of payrolls.
